stories.headline: Zelda's remake just smashed a record.
stories.body: Nintendo says the <mark>Ocarina of Time remake</mark> sold <mark>5.2 million copies</mark> in its first <mark>four days</mark>, through Nov 9. That makes it the <mark>fastest-selling first-party Switch 2 game</mark> so far. It's a <mark>Switch 2 exclusive</mark>.

stories.headline: Google made an AI that only answers yes or no.
stories.body: The new <mark>Gemini Decisions API</mark> scores options instead of writing text. It handles up to <mark>1,000 questions per request</mark> in about <mark>150-250 ms</mark>, for <mark>$0.10 per million input tokens</mark>. There's a <mark>free tier</mark> to try it.

stories.headline: DeepMind's new AI reads DNA better.
stories.body: <mark>AlphaGenome 2</mark> predicts how DNA changes affect <mark>specific cell types</mark>. Google says it finds <mark>nearly twice as many</mark> variants that change gene activity. It's <mark>research-only</mark> and <mark>not approved for diagnosis</mark>.

stories.headline: SpaceX will try to catch two rockets.
stories.body: <mark>Starship Flight 15</mark> targets <mark>Fri, Nov 13</mark>, 5:45pm EST. The plan: catch the <mark>booster and the ship</mark> with the tower's arms, a <mark>first for an orbital ship</mark>. The date <mark>can slip</mark> and catches can be called off.
